facts.text: Hampton claims to be the oldest continuously occupied English settlement in the U.S., founded after Jamestown was abandoned in 1699.
The city was named for Henry Wriothesley, 3rd Earl of Southampton, whose name also graces the Hampton River and Hampton Roads.
Founded in 1610, Hampton was the first continuous English‑speaking settlement, America's first free public education, and the training ground for NASA’s first astronauts.
Fort Monroe, built by Christopher Newport in 1607, sits on Old Point Comfort and later became a National Monument under President Obama.
During the Civil War, Fort Monroe sheltered “Contraband” slaves, leading to the Grand Contraband Camp, the first self‑contained African‑American community in the U.S.
The Grand Contraband Camp’s residents helped establish Hampton University, home of the famous Emancipation Oak that witnessed the 1863 Emancipation Proclamation.
